candidate_sources.README.md:
# Transit stop lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Module cache and EventTarget subscription handles; actual Node16 promises

checkpoints: On removal of the final observer, distinguish an online-mode attempt that remained paused and never entered queryFn from unconsumed work that already started.
Before reconnect queues or executes paused continuation, verify that the originating attempt is still authorized to enter queryFn.
In an already-queued continuation callback, recheck attempt identity and cancellation/settlement before invoking queryFn.
If queryFn is entered after the final observer has departed, its lazily accessed AbortSignal must not be live.
Verify the repair with refetchOnReconnect both enabled and disabled because the defect is explicitly independent of that option.
forbidden_effects: Do not allow the described departed, never-started offline attempt to consume a live AbortSignal after reconnect.
Do not let a queued continuation bypass final-observer cancellation merely because the attempt has recorded zero failures.
Do not cancel every unobserved attempt: unconsumed active work is allowed to finish into the shared cache.
Do not make late fulfillment from an obsolete attempt become a newer attempt's data.
Do not change public interfaces, dependencies, build/test configuration, or non-product files.
lifecycle_identity: The relevant lifecycle is the native query object and its specific Attempt object, not merely the key or injected callback handle.
Session.active(q,a), defined as q.attempt===a&&!a.settled, is the existing attempt-generation authority and must continue to reject replaced or settled attempts.
Observer handles identify subscriptions; losing the final handle is the departure boundary for the described fresh paused attempt.
The attempt's AbortController owns the signal exposed to that attempt's queryFn.

obligations.text: A fresh online-mode query subscribed and unsubscribed while offline must not later call its signal-consuming queryFn with a live signal when connectivity returns.
The protection in O1 must apply independently of refetchOnReconnect.
Final-observer departure must invalidate or cancel the described paused, never-entered attempt strongly enough to cover both future reconnect scheduling and continuation work already queued.
Continuation callbacks must remain bound to the originating query and Attempt identity, and settled or replaced attempts must produce no query invocation or completion effects.

Preserve legitimate shared-cache behavior: multiple observers share one fetch, active unconsumed work may finish after a view departs, consumed work remains physically abortable, and supported network modes and retry behavior remain intact.

Preserve cancellation restoration and freshness behavior: cancellation restores the attempt's previous query state with idle fetch status, settles the originating attempt, and late fulfillment cannot populate a replacement attempt.
Change product source only while preserving public interfaces, dependencies, and build/test configuration.

ordering_barriers: Final-observer departure must take effect before a later reconnect can authorize the paused attempt's initial queryFn entry.
A queued Promise continuation must check current attempt authority and departure cancellation after it begins executing and before this.invoke(q,a).
Attempt cancellation must mark the attempt settled and restore state before abort-driven or late asynchronous completion can publish effects.

The lazy signal getter records consumption synchronously when queryFn reads context.signal; therefore protection must exist before any prohibited queryFn entry or must ensure any signal exposed there is already canceled.
preservation: Keep subscribe(key,options), unique observer handles, unsubscribe(handle), online(value), focus(value), snapshot(key), and dispose().
Keep query status, fetchStatus, and data semantics, including synchronous initial online entry and Promise-turn resumption of paused work.
Keep network-mode behavior: online mode waits for connectivity, always may run offline, and offlineFirst may enter once offline while a retry can pause.
Keep retry scheduler usage and focus eligibility for continuation.
Keep multiple-observer fetch sharing and inert handling of unknown unsubscribe handles.
Keep the cache outside individual observer scopes and allow unconsumed work that has already started to finish into it after a view departs.
Keep consumed work abortable, cancellation state restoration, and rejection of late fulfillment from obsolete attempts.
Keep snapshot isolation through returning a copied state object.
scope: Product behavior in src/session.js for subscription departure, paused-attempt cancellation, reconnect/focus resumption, queued continuation, and signal ownership.
The precise defect is a fresh online-mode attempt that remains offline from mount through unmount and is later resumed after reconnect.
README.md and TASK define supported behavior; VISIBLE_CHECKS.md defines only public syntax/build checks and does not add business behavior.

active(q,a){return q.attempt===a&&!a.settled;}
cancel(q,a){if(a.settled)return;a.settled=true;q.state={...a.previous,fetchStatus:'idle'};a.controller.abort();this.project(q);}
Object.defineProperty(context,'signal',{enumerable:true,get(){q.consumed=true;return a.controller.signal;}});

resume(q){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&this.active(q,a)&&q.state.fetchStatus==='paused'&&this.eligible(a)&&!a.queued){a.queued=true;Promise.resolve().then(()=>{a.queued=false;if(!this.active(q,a))return;if(a.failures&&a.retryCancelled){a.settled=true;q.state={...q.state,status:'error',fetchStatus:'idle'};this.project(q);return;}this.invoke(q,a);});}}
if(q.observers.size===0){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)this.cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}
These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract already captures the original defect and preservation constraints, so there is no supported contract gap. The previous candidate appears to address the specified boundary by recording whether queryFn has started and canceling an unsettled attempt on final-observer departure when it has not started or its signal was consumed. Cancellation settles the attempt, restores its prior state, and causes the queued resume callback's existing active-identity check to return before invocation. The supplied acceptance failure contains no cause and cannot establish an implementation gap. Therefore neither a defect nor correctness can be conclusively inferred from the permitted evidence, and the proper classification is unknown.

routing_analysis.contract: A per-key shared cache owns query state while observer handles own only subscriptions. Each fetch attempt owns its controller, completion, consumption state, and generation identity. A fresh online-mode attempt may pause offline, but final-observer departure must invalidate that never-started attempt before reconnect or a queued Promise continuation can enter queryFn. Started, unconsumed work may continue into the shared cache; consumed work is abortable. Every async continuation and completion must remain authorized by native query/Attempt identity. Cancellation settles the originating attempt, restores its prior state with idle fetch status, and prevents late fulfillment from affecting a replacement. The repair is independent of refetchOnReconnect and must preserve interfaces, network modes, retries, dependencies, and configuration.
